parts.content:
I have found and used existing syntheses relevant to simulation for training and evaluating driving policies to draft a literature review. The draft is titled "Simulation for Training and Evaluating Driving Policies" (ID: 675d9ecd-6fb9-5516-a3ac-525fb4f56fcd). 

This review covers:
- The use of mid-level input representations and recurrent neural network (ChauffeurNet) for autonomous driving, facilitating training on real or simulated data and closed-loop simulation testing before real deployment.
- The CARLA open-source urban driving simulator that supports development, training, and validation of autonomous driving models with flexible sensor and environmental specifications, as well as compliance measurements.
- Comparison of ChauffeurNet's approach with an end-to-end convolutional neural network (CNN) method that learns the entire processing pipeline from raw images.
- Insights into how simulation platforms like CARLA complement mid-level representation methods for safer development workflows.
- Identification of contradictions between end-to-end CNN and mid-level RNN approaches in input-output representations.
- A noted gap in the literature due to lack of direct comparative evaluation of the CNN and RNN methods under the same conditions.

If you want, I can provide the full text or help with anything else related to this review.
